checks.name: transition-table-over-every-command-kind
checks.summary: A3, asserted as a table over EVERY axis rather than a sample. Validate accepts both a recorded and a zero CapturedAt for all 11 RequirementStatus values (the axis is reused from invariant_model_test.go's allRequirementStatuses() and guarded against drift by wantRequirementStatusCount, not re-declared). All 9 RequirementCommandKind values pass through DecideRequirement leaving CapturedAt byte-identical -- compared on Equal, on Unix seconds, on nanoseconds AND on location name, because the persisted form is the representation -- and each kind is driven from a start status where it is a LEGAL transition, with the status change and the version bump asserted first so the table cannot pass vacuously on refusals. The command's own At is a different instant, so a branch overwriting CapturedAt with command.At would be caught; an unknown kind is still refused. A legacy (zero) record stays legacy through every kind: no transition invents a capture time. CompleteRequirementFromRelease, driven with a real StableReleaseProof minted through PromoteRelease/Permit/CompletePromotionWithProof, leaves the value byte-identical and leaves a legacy record legacy. A fourth test reads model.go's AST and pins Requirement's field list to exactly ID, Status, Version, Increments, StableSnapshot, RequestedBy, CapturedAt with zero struct tags on the struct.

checks.name: legacy-record-is-valid
checks.summary: A6's domain half: a Requirement with a zero CapturedAt is VALID for every status, so no record written before the field existed becomes unreadable, and CaptureRecorded() reports false for it and true for a non-zero value. This is V2-052's RequestedBy precedent on the same struct, and the reason it matters more here is recorded in model.go's own comment: the zero time.Time marshals to a real-looking instant in the year 1, which an ordering rule that rewards age reads as maximally old and therefore maximally privileged.
